newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel says eases up on "internal closure".
newsitem.headline: Israel says eases up on "internal closure".

text.p: Israel on Wednesday announced a slight easing of a security clampdown on Palestinians within the West Bank and Gaza Strip but said a week-old ban on entering the Jewish state remained in force.
An army statement said Palestinians had been allowed since Wednesday morning to reach workplaces at Jewish settlements and industrial zones in the two areas.
"Likewise from this morning, it was permitted to bring in raw supplies for industry in the West Bank and Gaza Strip and essential goods to the Gaza Strip," the statement said.

The step marked some easing of an "internal closure" on the movement of Palestinians between towns and villages in the West Bank and Gaza imposed as part of an Israeli clampdown following last Wednesday's twin suicide bombing in Jerusalem.
But the statement made clear there would be no let-up in preventing Palestinians from entering Israel.
"It is stressed that the full closure of the West Bank and Gaza continues and it is forbidden for Palestinian workers to enter Israel," the statement said.

Israel sealed off the West Bank and Gaza Strip after last Wednesday's bombing killed 15 people including the two Arab bombers in a Jerusalem street market. Palestinian President Yasser Arafat condemned the closure as collective punishment.

Crown Prince Hassan of Jordan failed in talks with Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu in Jerusalem on Wednesday to persuade Israel to end its package of sanctions, imposed to try to pressure Arafat to get tough with Islamic militants.
"If they begin to fight terrorism, we will review the various steps that were taken in order to make them fight terrorism," Netanyahu said after the meeting.
Netanyahu said it was not Israel's intention to inflict "undue suffering" on Palestinians and it had allowed humanitarian supplies into self-ruled areas.
An army spokeswoman said Palestinian workers would need permission to reach their jobs in the West Bank and Gaza Strip. She was unable to say how many workers were affected by Wednesday's action.
